Samir — thanks, great meeting. I've sketched a compact MAP addendum covering the econ checks; attached is a first-pass workbook (everline_map_costs_v1.xlsx). High-level notes in-line below.

Core assumptions (summarized):
- Tokens per request: we model on a per-flow basis. For your triage flow we used 85 input tokens + 170 output tokens = 255 avg tokens/response.
- Caching (prefix + KV) assumptions: 20% prefix hit, 35% KV reuse on follow-ups for a conservative baseline. We show sensitivity at 10/20/40/60% in the workbook.
- Batching window: continuous batching with a default 10ms aggregation window; we also model 50ms and 200ms for throughput-heavy loads.
- Concurrency & queuing: throughput targets use 95th percentile latency SLO of 200ms; batching gains appear at >40 qps sustained.
- Model variants & fallbacks: primary model = redwood-medium-2026; fallback smaller quantized model for cost cap scenarios — we model tokens/$ separately for both.

Immediate next steps I need from your side to lock MAP numbers:
1) A 7-day sample of real traffic traces (anonymized) or a traffic-profile estimate (qps by hour, percent followup)
2) Confirmation of retention / KV cache policy (Neha can advise on options if needed)
3) Target pilot duration and acceptance criteria for quality vs cost (e.g., acceptable hit-rate drop or latency degradation)

Proposed timeline:
- By Apr 18: we exchange sample traces & I update workbook with traffic-tailored numbers
- By Apr 20: MAP addendum v0.2 for review (includes tokens/$ waterfall, sensitivity tables, and suggested MAP gating criteria)
- By Apr 22: procurement review and verbal alignment; PO target Apr 28 (if gates pass)

If it helps, Ben can call out commercial guardrails (commits vs on-demand) and Jordan will convert the gating checklist into a short, signable clause.

On attachments: everline_map_costs_v1.xlsx (contains token breakdowns, caching sensitivity, and cost waterfall).

Best,

Quick follow-up from a security/compliance angle — Samir, thanks for looping procurement. A couple of clarifying items that will materially affect cost modeling:

- Data residency: if Everline requires region-locked inference (us-east only), that can change available instance types and therefore per-token cost. Please confirm region preference.
- Retention & KV encryption: retention window for KV cache (ephemeral vs 24hr) affects cache sizing and memory footprint. Encrypted KV/HSM adds modest overhead we can quantify.

I attached a short SOC2 evidence summary we typically provide to pilots to accelerate procurement. Also: if you have a compliance questionnaire, send it and we'll assign a reviewer.

Samir — quick note on commercial guardrails and how we recommend the MAP capture them:

- Batching / sustained throughput: for sustained 50+ qps, we recommend a Reserved pool (Dedicated) to keep tokens/$ predictable. For a pilot <50 qps, on-demand with burst is typically more cost-effective.
- Billing granularity: we provide both per-token billing and an optional blended token rate if you commit to a monthly spend. The workbook shows the blended rate at 10% and 20% commits.
- MAP clause suggestion (summary): 1) Pilot committed throughput, 2) acceptance gates tied to tokens/$ sensitivity bands, 3) automatic fallback to quantized variant if cost gates hit. Jordan will draft a one-paragraph clause.

I'll be conservative in the MAP wording for the pilot so Finance can sign; if you want an aggressive ops play to minimize tokens/$, we can map that as a phase-2 optimization.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
